restrictions: Generic distinguished-point birthday collision search on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family; no cryptanalytic weakness in 40-round SHA-256 is claimed and no full-width 256-bit collision is produced.

Full-width success probability (>= 0.390001) relies on H1-random-function-walk; all body, outer-controller, and unrolled 2-lane SIMD recovery bytecode records are concretely emitted and executed on the declared 256-bit word-RAM VM in experiments/sha256_r40_search.py.

heuristics.statement: The iterated 256-bit Walk-B transition F(Y) = B(Y) XOR PD on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family of 40-round SHA-256 behaves like a uniform random function on {0,1}^256 with respect to birthday collision hazard, distinguished-point hitting times (p = 2145 / 2^122), trail-length tails, and 47-bit key independence.
heuristics.scope: Complete 40-round SHA-256 (steps 0..39 on every padded block, standard FIPS 180-4 IV, padding, message schedule, and feed-forward) restricted to 64-byte messages with fixed 8-word prefix W[0..7] and affine offsets W[8+k] = Y_k - K[8+k] (k=2..7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Extrapolated from the van Oorschot-Wiener (1999) and Flajolet-Odlyzko (1990) random-function birthday theory together with two organizer-executed reduced-width experiments on the 64-byte W[0..7]-prefix 2-block digest map at w=16 (merging bounded DP walk, strict total budget max_evals=285, dp_bits=2) and w=14 (fixed-budget M=127 collision rate near P=0.39), plus a direct 64-trial w=12 iterated Walk-B F(Y) birthday check executed on the native 5-byte RecProg VM inside selftest().
heuristics.limitations: Reduced-width empirical experiments at w=12, 14, and 16 cannot prove the absence of structural correlations or non-random cycle behavior in F(Y) at full 256-bit width. If 40-round SHA-256 deviated significantly from a random function under F, the achieved success probability could fall below 0.39.
